title: FBI Director Kash Patel says the agency is leaving its D.C. headquarters
summary: Maryland lawmakers and FBI Director Kash Patel agree on at least one thing -- the agency's headquarters in Washington, D.C., has to go. After that, they still disagree on where the new HQ should be, with Maryland lawmakers pushing for Greenbelt.
content:
By Grace Newton

Maryland lawmakers and FBI Director Kash Patel appear to agree on at least one thing — the agency’s current headquarters in Washington, D.C., has to go.

After that, they continue to disagree.

Patel called the current headquarters, the J. Edgar Hoover Building on Pennsylvania Avenue, “unsafe for our workforce” and said in a brief interview Friday on Fox’s “Mornings with Maria” and said the staff would be moving out.

The move would transfer 1,500 employees to various locations across the country.

“The FBI has 38,000 when we’re fully manned, which we’re not. In the national capital region, in the 50-mile radius around Washington, D.C., there were 11,000 FBI employees,” Patel told Fox. “That’s like a third of the workforce. A third of the crime doesn’t happen here, so we’re taking 1,500 of those folks and moving them out.”

Patel didn’t say where the new headquarters may be located. But Maryland lawmakers say that question has already been answered.

After a 15-year debate, the FBI announced in November a move to Greenbelt, but President Trump said earlier this year that he planned to halt that relocation.

“They need a new headquarters. Greenbelt has already been selected — we’re the fastest track to get something done, we’ve got a site that’s ready to go, we’ve got funding set aside to do it,” said Rep. Glenn Ivey (D4th), whose district includes the Greenbelt site.

Trump wants to keep FBI headquarters in D.C. , not ‘three hours away in Maryland’

“I agree with him [Patel] about getting out of the D.C. location. Come out here, we can make it happen faster than any place else in the country,” Ivey said.

But D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser said in a statement to WTOP that the FBI headquarters being in the city “keeps America safer.”

“The District and our region have many sites where the FBI can fulfill their mission in safe, modern, and secure facilities, and we are ready to help them find both temporary leases and a permanent home,” Bowser wrote.

“A safe and beautiful D.C. requires a committed federal partner that will keep our Nation’s Capital a symbol of American strength,” she wrote.

Bowser was seemingly referring to Trump’s executive order from March that vowed to make the nation’s capital “safe, beautiful and prosperous” by creating a task force made up of members from several federal agencies to address crime and immigration policies.

Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen said that there’s some confusion around which employees Patel wants to move.

“Over 900 of those are vacant positions, where they’re going to be moving those positions to other offices around the country, including, for example, 40 additional FBI officers in Baltimore. So, that is not an issue,” Van Hollen said. “These are vacant positions.

“With respect to the other maybe 500, that will require congressional notification and ultimately Congress, if we’re together, can decide to approve or not approve,” he said.

While the move seems like a no-brainer to Ivey, it’s hard to predict the administration’s next move.

“It’s hard to be confident with anything with the Trump administration, because you never know what they’re going to do,” Ivey said. “But, this is an easy one from a standpoint of following the law and taking the path of least resistance. It’s already been laid out after 15 years of work to get this done.”

The FBI told WTOP they have no additional comments on the matter.
author: WTOP News
